explain.say: Why 24 hours in a day, and not 10 or 20? The answer starts in ancient Egypt, at the first point of the timeline. At night, Egyptians watched 12 groups of stars rise one after another, and each one marked an hour of darkness.

faq.q: Why did the Egyptians split the night into 12?
faq.a: They watched groups of stars, called decans, rise through the night. About 12 of them marked the dark hours, so the night got 12 hours.

faq.q: Were hours always the same length?
faq.a: No. For thousands of years an hour was one twelfth of the daylight, so day hours were long in summer and short in winter.

faq.q: When did all hours become equal?
faq.a: Astronomers used equal hours from Greek times, but everyday life switched when mechanical clocks spread through European towns in the 1300s.

faq.q: How many seconds are in a day?
faq.a: 86,400. That is 24 hours times 60 minutes times 60 seconds.
Very nearly. Earth's spin changes by tiny fractions of a second, so timekeepers have sometimes added a leap second to keep clocks in step.

facts: Ancient Egyptian hours were seasonal, with day hours longer in summer than in winter.
